'''The Wheel Turns: Jordan at Work''' is the third chapter of {{origins}}.

The chapter covers how [[Robert Jordan]] initially conceived of ''[[The Wheel of Time]]'', how he got published, and his process for writing the books. Some of the themes and symbolism of the series are also discussed.

The chapter includes a smattering of detailed accounts of the inspiration, origin, and development of various terms, names, and other details within the series. Of particular note is a section addressing the so-called "[[Mazrim Taim#Taimandred|Taimandred]]" fan theory that [[Mazrim Taim]] was [[Demandred]] in disguise.

{{Quote|quote=So when Jordan was starting to write ''[[Lord of Chaos]]'', he indeed ''thought'' Mazrim Taim was the Forsaken Demandred in disguise. He recorded as much in his private notes, in which he twice noted that “Taim/Demandred showed up” at [[Dumai’s Wells]]. He even underscored and put it in bold font when he was summing up the works of the Forsaken so far:|speakers=Michael Livingston|other_refs={{ref/book|origins|3}}}}
{{Quote|quote=Demandred: Hated/feared/despised Lews Therin. Like Lanfear, he plays for larger stakes than most of the others, who are trying to stake out worldly kingdoms. HE WILL SHOW UP CLAIMING TO BE '''<u>MAZRIM TAIM</u>''', TAKING ADVANTAGE OF RAND’S AMNESTY.|speakers=Robert Jordan|other_refs={{ref/rignotes|58|6|15|People}}{{ref/book|origins|3}}}}

The chapter also covers ''{{Wiki|The White Goddess}}'' as an overall source of inspiration for ''The Wheel of Time''.
